status: Current production mapping/filtering passed stateful controls and fixed-frame checks. Experimental zero-copy remains disabled; its HDR image equivalence is unproven. No new player performance result.
method: Three separate native processes, each one long-lived player through twelve stages: initial H264, zoom/unzoom, rotate/unrotate, explicit rgba8/auto, software/hardware decode replacement, HDR replacement/SDR return, stop/reopen. Original pipeline = direct NV12 off and default copy mapping. Candidate = direct NV12 on and default copy mapping. Experimental = direct NV12 on and zero-copy mapping. Same bundled DLL, balanced scaling, GPU timing off, four vertex cache entries and one hardware decoder thread. Each capture is paused at exactly 2s; load events are drained/awaited to exclude stale properties. Actual decoder and redraw-path descriptions checked per stage; all owner windows stayed hidden. No CPU, RAM, startup, throughput or visible-cadence performance measurement. No VLC process.

pairedSdrCases.scope: Each SDR stage versus the original pipeline, including fallback and restoration. One channel level out of 255 maximum.

returnConsistency.scope: Six restored stages versus the initial H264 frame in each of three processes; exact pixels.

captureProtection.scope: Existing prefix intentionally rejected, expected failure exit and twelve unchanged PNG hashes.

experimentalZeroCopyDecision.finding: Earlier single-run linear-profile screen removed repeated view creation (745 hits, 12 created views) but still used more recorded CPU than the copy path. It is a different older DLL/profile and is not a fresh comparison of the balanced app. This validation also observes a 40-level HDR capture difference in the experimental zero-copy sequence. These data do not justify adoption.
experimentalZeroCopyDecision.hdrCause: Unresolved. The observation does not isolate decoder-surface mapping/layout from adaptive HDR peak history. It must not be attributed to the direct NV12 filter, which was on its original fallback path for HDR.

captures.note: Byte-identical captures share one stored PNG; all original stage SHA256/size mappings are preserved. All original files remain in the external scratch directory.

limits: Correctness validation does not prove a CPU/RAM win or visible presentation cadence. Existing performance history/VLC baseline are unchanged.
HDR was observed and reported, not subjected to an invented universal tolerance; current default mapping matched its baseline, experimental zero-copy did not.
The experimental native view cache was not rebuilt or enabled, and zero-copy is not enabled in App source.
This is not a new full app unit/regression gate. Previous validation remains separate evidence.
nextPerformanceInvestigation: The native recipe uses FFmpeg --enable-small and size-optimized mpv/libplacebo builds. Evaluate a separate reproducible compiler/codec performance candidate against matching software-decode correctness and internal CPU work before considering adoption; no benefit has been measured yet.
